title: Robust streaming structured-output: fragment markers, reassembly, and SDK compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers rely on streaming structured outputs (JSON objects, function/tool call payloads) for low-latency pipelines. In practice we see three high-risk edge cases during streaming: (1) escape sequences split across chunk boundaries (e.g. a backslash at end-of-chunk), (2) truncated multi-byte UTF-8 characters or nested JSON fragments when early truncation / connection drop occurs, and (3) retry/resume semantics that must be compatible with older SDKs that expect newline-delimited JSON events rather than our newer framed metadata model. These cause unparsable JSON on the client, lost function call arguments, and difficulty implementing safe resume/retry.

Scope: Define a server-side streaming framing augmentation and a minimal, backwards-compatible client-facing contract that enables safe reassembly, explicit continuation indicators, and a deterministic retry/resume mechanism. This ticket covers the protocol design, runtime changes to emit metadata with each chunk, SDK compatibility behaviors, tests, and rollout plan. Implementation of SDK adapters will be separate tickets.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Add a small, explicit per-chunk metadata envelope to streaming events. Each envelope is still text-based and prefix-sent so legacy newline-delimited SDKs can ignore metadata if they choose. The envelope fields we will emit (as ASCII-safe tokens, not nested JSON) are: CHUNK_ID, OFFSET, FRAG_FLAG, CHECKSUM. Example prefix: "<<RI:CHUNK id=42 off=184 FRAG=1 csum=2b7>>" followed immediately by the chunk payload bytes. FRAG_FLAG=1 means this chunk is a continuation fragment (not a complete logical JSON object).

2) Continuation semantics: clients/SDKs will concatenate payloads in order of OFFSET and re-run JSON parsing when either FRAG_FLAG=0 (end-of-object) or EOF is signaled. On reconnect, the client may request resume from the last acknowledged OFFSET. Server will provide a lightweight, ephemeral resume token for streaming sessions to allow replay from a byte offset for up to 60s.

3) Escapes and UTF-8: The runtime will ensure we never split inside a UTF-8 code point when emitting a chunk boundary. For escape sequences specifically (e.g. backslash followed by quote), we will treat a trailing backslash at the end of a chunk as FRAG_FLAG=1 and let the continuation assemble the full escape before parsing. This avoids ambiguous partial escapes on the client.

4) Backwards compatibility: Older SDKs that only expect newline-delimited JSON should still be able to operate: we will keep emitting fully-formed newline-delimited JSON events when the model produces small, complete objects; for large or fragmented outputs we will still include the ASCII envelope prefixed on its own line. Older SDKs will see the envelope as an extra line; we will document the envelope format and provide SDK adapters. Newer SDKs can parse the envelope to implement robust reassembly and resume.

5) Deterministic retries: When a client reconnects and asks to resume from OFFSET X, the server will replay chunks starting from the earliest chunk with offset >= X and include the same CHUNK_ID/OFFSET values to allow exact reassembly. The ephemeral resume token ties the client session to server buffer retention. If the buffer is expired, the server returns a specific error (RESUME_EXPIRED) and the client falls back to a full fresh request.

6) Function/tool arguments: For tool calling we will treat the function-call payload as a single logical object that may be fragmented across multiple chunks. The reassembly rules ensure the final assembled string is valid JSON before being forwarded to tool invocation. If resume is impossible and the assembled payload is incomplete, the server will cancel the function call and emit an explicit error event so SDKs can surface a clear retry or fallback path.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- ASCII envelope vs binary framing: ASCII prefix keeps the wire human-readable and avoids breaking simple clients. It adds minimal overhead and is easy to ignore for legacy clients.
- Server buffer retention window (60s): short enough to limit memory footprint, long enough for common intermittent network retries. Longer retention improves resilience but increases resources.
- Forcing UTF-8-safe boundaries slightly complicates runtime emission code (must inspect upcoming bytes), but eliminates a class of client parse failures.

Open questions (to be resolved in design review):
- Should we use cryptographic checksum or lightweight crc32 for CHECKSUM? (crc32 preferred initially for speed.)
- Exact token syntax for the envelope to avoid collisions with user text (we propose the unlikely prefix <<RI:CHUNK ).
- Resume token lifetime and quotas for heavy concurrent streams.

Implementation notes:
- Runtime: modify streamer to compute OFFSETS per-chunk, ensure UTF-8-safe split, emit envelope line + payload. Add ephemeral resume store keyed by session id.
- Console/observability: add per-stream metrics: fragments_emitted, resumes_attempted, resume_failures, fragmented_function_calls.
- SDK: add adapters for Node/Python/Go to parse envelope, reassemble, and expose a stable event for completed JSON objects and function call boundaries.

References and artifacts:
- Design doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Streaming+Fragment+Protocol
- Prototype PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4862
- SDK adapter sketch (node): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/351
- Incident notes: https://redwood.ai/incident/2025-12-stream-json-fail

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Older clients may misinterpret envelope lines as events. Mitigation: envelope line uses an unlikely prefix and documentation; SDK adapters will strip it.
- Risk: resume token leakage. Mitigation: short TTL and tokens are single-use for replay.
- Risk: increased CPU for checksum and UTF-8 inspection. Mitigation: benchmarked in PR; costs small vs parsing errors avoided.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge runtime support behind feature flag (FF_stream_frag_reassembly=false by default).
2) Deploy to canary region and run synthetic workloads with fuzzed boundary cases for 48h.
3) Release SDK adapters in parallel and publish migration guide.
4) Turn feature flag on for 20% traffic, monitor console metrics and error rates for 1 week.
5) Full rollout if stable.

Acceptance criteria:
- Server emits envelope-prefixed fragments for fragmented outputs when feature flag enabled.
- SDK adapters can reassemble fragments and produce valid JSON objects for 100k fuzzed boundary cases with zero parse failures.
- Resume from OFFSET successfully replays identical CHUNK_ID/OFFSET pairs for at least 60s window in canary.
- Observability shows fragment-related errors reduced or made actionable (clear RESUME_EXPIRED vs parse error).

acceptance_criteria: Envelope is emitted for fragmented streams and can be ignored by legacy clients without causing parse errors
SDK adapters (node/python/go) can reassemble fragments and return valid JSON objects for injected partial-escape and UTF-8 truncation tests
Resume API replays chunks deterministically for tokens within TTL; expired tokens yield RESUME_EXPIRED
Function/tool invocation receives either a fully-formed JSON payload or an explicit failed-invocation event (never a silent partial)
